steps.title: In the ground

form.name: Dysprosium in ion-adsorption clay
form.label: about 7% of the rare earths in the richest clays

steps.text: The seventeen rare earths always occur together, never alone. The heavy ones, dysprosium among them, are scarce in the hard-rock ores. Their main source is ion-adsorption clay in southern China and Myanmar, where they cling loosely to weathered granite. In bastnäsite and monazite it is well under 1%.
steps.india: Monazite is poor in dysprosium. Lignite ash at Neyveli holds about 2,100 mg/kg of rare earths, and a pilot is planned.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: No digging is needed for the clays. A salt solution, usually ammonium sulphate, is pumped into the hillside; it washes the rare earths off the clay and drains out at the bottom, where they are precipitated as a mixed carbonate. The method is cheap and can foul soil and water.
steps.india: 2,900 tonnes of rare-earth oxide in 2025, 0.7% of the world, all from monazite in beach sands worked by IREL.

steps.title: Dissolve
steps.text: The mixed carbonate from the clays is dissolved in hydrochloric acid and filtered. There is no hard mineral to break down, and little of the thorium that comes with monazite. What is left is a mixed rare-earth chloride: all the elements still together.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: This is the hard part. Neighbouring rare earths behave almost identically, so the solution is run through hundreds of solvent-extraction stages, each shifting the balance slightly, until dysprosium comes out on its own as an oxide. China does about 91% of the world's separation.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Dysprosium oxide is reduced to metal or to a dysprosium-iron alloy. Magnet makers add it to NdFeB, increasingly by diffusing it along the grain boundaries of a finished magnet, which uses far less.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: A few per cent of dysprosium lets an NdFeB magnet keep its strength at the 150 to 200°C found inside electric-vehicle motors and wind-turbine generators. Without it the magnet fades as it heats.
steps.india: IREL wants to buy 300 tonnes of dysprosium oxide (expression of interest, February 2026).

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Grinding dust and offcuts from magnet factories are reprocessed. Magnets in old motors, drives and turbines are rarely recovered yet: they are small, glued in and scattered across many products.
